00 — Tagline

Canonical tagline

Easy, fast and safe way to trade crypto.

Approved variants

Full form — primary

Easy, fast and safe way to trade crypto.

Landing hero, About page, paid ad headlines, OG meta, App Store / Google Play descriptions, _config.yml site description, SEO meta description, press boilerplate.

Short form

Easy, fast and safe.

Three-word lockup for icon rows, social bio, footer strap, T-shirt prints. Always set in three commas-then-and order, never reordered.

Pillar attribute set

Easy · Fast · Safe

Feature-row label set. Each maps to a product proof: Easy → instant AUD on/off-ramp via Osko/PayID. Fast → under-1-minute deposits. Safe → AUSTRAC VASP, 2FA, cold storage.

Punctuation & capitalisation

Comma — single Oxford-style comma between "Easy" and "fast". No serial comma before "and safe".
Lowercase — "easy", "fast", "safe", "way", "trade", "crypto" all lowercase in body context. Sentence-case at the start of a sentence ("Easy, fast and safe..."). All-caps treatment only in micro-contexts (badges, labels < 14px).
Full stop — include when the tagline ends a paragraph or sits alone. Drop the full stop when the tagline is set inline in a sentence or as a button/CTA label.
Emphasis — when highlighting one word, italicise or colour-shift the first three ("Easy, fast and safe") never the last clause.

Do & don't

Do

  • Use the full form on every public-facing surface where there's room.
  • Pair with a single specific proof (zero fees, instant AUD, AUSTRAC, 24/7 support) — not three.
  • Set in Poppins, 600–700 weight, generous letter-spacing.
  • Treat the tagline as a sentence: capital E at start, full stop at end (where context allows).
  • Keep "Easy", "fast" and "safe" in that order — the rhythm is the brand.

Don't

  • Reorder — never "Fast, safe and easy" or "Safe, easy and fast".
  • Add adjectives — not "Easy, fast, safe and cheap" or "The easiest, fastest, safest...".
  • Translate inside a single en-AU asset — English only on AU surfaces.
  • Use as a verb claim ("We make crypto easy, fast and safe") — keep it as a noun-phrase descriptor.
  • Combine with hype phrases ("Easy, fast and safe — to the moon").

Logo rules: The icon mark is the "C" letterform + keyhole shape — paths 1 and 2 from LogoIcon.tsx, viewBox 0 0 30 35. The keyhole fill is always --rgb-landing-keyhole-color (#1AADFF) — never changes. The C letterform is white on dark surfaces, #00233A on light. Never recolour, rotate, distort, or shadow. Maintain clear space equal to the cap-height of "C" on all sides. Known gap: the border does not currently render. .btn sets border: none, and the outline rule sets only border-color, so production computes 0px none and the button reads as flat transparent. Restoring it needs a width and style on the outline rule.
Dark — landing nav only

Outline pill — row actions

Button geometry

weight500, always, from --button-font-weight. Never write the number inline — the token is defined in both themes, and hardcoded weights are how the primary button spent a long time rendering lighter than the outline button beside it.
size16px text · 50px tall · 8px 24px padding.
radius8px on app buttons. Landing CTAs use 3px — a deliberate difference between the marketing surface and the app, not drift.
landing CTAsRendered as <a class="landing-button">, so they inherit nothing from .btn. A top-level .landing-button rule carries the weight; without it they fall back to the browser default of 400.
disabledOpacity 0.65. A disabled button must say why it is disabled — put the reason in the label ("Not enough BTC"), not in a tooltip.

06 — UI patterns

The clean-card style (website and app, Oct 2026)

  • Cards: white on the grey page, 16px radius, soft --card-shadow, no border, 20px padding. Panels inside a card use 12px.
  • Hairlines, not boxes: dividers and outlines use --hairline (primary text at 8%).
  • Tables: muted sentence-case headers, faint hairline row dividers, no zebra stripes, tabular numerals right-aligned.
  • Tabs: text tabs with a thin #0078F0 underline on the active one.
  • Stats: small muted label (--text-muted, 62%) with a bold figure; stacked in cards, label then figure on one row in compact bars.
  • Pills: filters, timeframes and toggles are outlined pills; the active one is outlined in #0078F0 with a 1px inset ring, never a solid fill.
  • Selected rows: a soft blue tint with semibold text, never a solid blue bar.
  • Status and steps: a soft tint of the state colour with the colour as the text (verified green, pending gold, rejected red), never a solid block.
  • Pickers and dropdowns: the same white card with a hairline and soft shadow, a hairline search field with a small muted icon. Never a CTA-blue frame.
  • Balances: hideable with the eye toggle; a balance beside an amount field is labelled Available.
  • Price chart: market candles (Kraken) with dashed Buy (green) and Sell (red) lines at our live prices.

07 — Brand voice

Trustworthy
We speak plainly. AUSTRAC compliance and security are front and centre — never buried in fine print.
Accessible
Crypto can be complex. We explain it simply — welcoming newcomers without patronising experienced traders.
Confident
We are the reliable Australian choice. Direct and clear — free of hype, jargon, or inflated promises.
Local
Australian owned, AUSTRAC registered. We lead with our Australian identity — not a faceless global exchange.
Do

"Trade BTC, ETH, USDT and 40+ assets — zero fees, instant AUD deposits, backed by Australia's AUSTRAC-licensed exchange."

Don't

"MOON YOUR PORTFOLIO 🚀🚀 Join the CRYPTO REVOLUTION and get RICH with INSANE yields and 100x gains!!"

Two stacks send customer email today. Barong renders ERB templates from the repo (app/views/postmaster/) for account events; the connector sends SendGrid dynamic templates whose HTML lives in the SendGrid dashboard, referenced by id.

What barong actually sends (current production)

Production mailer templates live in the opendax repo — config/mailer/templates/ is mounted over barong's app/views/postmaster/ in the container, so the repo defaults never render. Eleven CoinPort-built templates (confirmation, password reset, session login notice, deposit, withdrawal with full record + blockchain TX tables, transfers, beneficiaries, labels) share the layout in config/mailer/mailer.html.erb, which signs off "©2026 CoinPort Pty Ltd. All rights reserved." Identical on the dev and prod branches. Edit templates there, not in barong.

Two tidy-ups, not emergencies. (1) The live layout footer carries only the copyright line — the standard on this page also wants the street address, AUSTRAC Registration #100633359 and ABN 12 624 879 223 in every customer email. (2) Barong's shadowed repo defaults still contain OpenDAX demo boilerplate ("Company Inc, 3 Abbey Road, San Francisco / opendax.io") — dead in deployment, but worth cleaning so a mount-less run can never regress to it (a rebrand branch exists in barong).

09 — Alerts & warnings

Feedback components for transactions, KYC, account security and system events. Each uses the colour token mapped to its semantic meaning — never reassign colours across states.

Inline alerts — light mode

Deposit received $2,500.00 AUD has cleared to your account. Available immediately. #4BC64A · --rgb-bids · Seagrass Green
Verify your identity Complete L3 KYC to unlock withdrawals above $10,000 AUD per day. #0078F0 · --rgb-primary-cta-color · Harbour Blue
Withdrawal pending review For your security, this $51,000 AUD withdrawal is being reviewed. ETA 2–4 hours. #FAC848 · --rgb-contrast-cta-color · Lantern Gold

Status pills

For transaction rows, account states, KYC tiers and order book entries.

Completed Verified Processing Pending review Action required Failed Cancelled Draft Archived
Semantic rules Success — only for completed positive actions (deposits cleared, orders filled, KYC approved). Never for ambient state.
Info — neutral notices and tips. Use for guidance, new features, sign-in alerts.
Warning — user attention required but no error: maintenance, pending review, 2FA prompts.
Danger — only for failures, rejections, security incidents. Never for low balance or "are you sure" prompts (use Warning).

10 — Spacing & grid

CoinPort spaces on a 5 pixel scale. Padding, margins and gaps are multiples of 5, with 10, 15 and 20 px carrying most of the interface. Container widths and gutters scale with viewport.

Two tokens exist in web/src/index.pcss: --gap: 6px, used inside calc() multipliers that set table row rhythm, and --big-gap: 60px. Everything else is written as a literal. A second family of 4, 8, 12 and 32 px runs through components inherited from Bootstrap — roughly a quarter of all spacing declarations. Prefer the 5 px scale in new work; do not convert existing Bootstrap-derived components purely to align them, because the table rhythm is derived arithmetically from the 6 px gap and re-deriving those multipliers is a layout change, not a tidy-up.

Container rules

max-width1080px — the widest content container, used by the market, learn, portfolio and quick exchange screens. Narrower screens cap at 900px; centred single-column forms and modals at 400–600px. Hero, nav and footer run full width.
gridBootstrap's 12 column grid, from the vendored stylesheet. There is no CoinPort grid of its own.
breakpoint768px is the layout switch throughout — below it the app serves its mobile components, not a reflowed desktop. 450px is the second-commonest query, for narrow phones.
page padding20px horizontal on content screens, 15px on mobile surfaces.
card padding15–20px internal padding inside card components.
full heightcalc(100vh - 60px) — the 60px is the header, measured: header.pg-header reports 60px signed in, and the landing header 60px at every width. No stylesheet declares it — the header is content-driven — so measure it in the running app before changing this number; a sweep in September assumed 65px and left several pages five pixels short. The value appears in seven stylesheets and they must agree.

Border radius

Field rules

Labels — always above the field, never floating placeholders. Required fields use a small asterisk in #FF617F.
Placeholders — show format hints only (e.g. "you@coinport.com.au"), never duplicate the label.
Validation — inline, immediately below the field, on blur (not as the user types). Error text in #FF617F; success in #4BC64A.
Focus ring — always visible for keyboard nav. 3px ring at 18% alpha on the primary CTA colour.
Spacing — 16px between fields, 8px between label and field. Field height: 40px (single line).

12 — Photography & illustration

CoinPort's primary visual language is flat illustration — the coastal/harbour landing scene. Photography is the secondary mode, used for editorial, blog, and PR. Both share the same restrained palette and treatment.

Primary — flat illustration

Coastal · daylight
Landing dayBoats, port-side buildings, mountains, AUS palette. Always behind hero headline.
Coastal · night
Landing nightSame harbour scene under stars and moon. Triggered by dark-mode toggle.
Editorial accent
Spot illustrationsCoin · vault · ship · key motifs. Solid fills, max 5 colours.

Page scenes — one harbour, a different time of day per page

The landing harbour is the backdrop for every marketing page (/buy, /sell, /swap, /coins, and the campaign pages /yourway, /local, /zerofees). Each page recolours the same scene and sky to its own time of day, so a customer can tell the pages apart at a glance while they still read as one place. Updated 31 Oct 2026.

PageDayNight
Landing Harbour Blue midday (the original scene) Night harbour, stars
/buy Mediterranean morning, navy text on a light sky Mediterranean night, lamp-lit town
/sell Warm Indian Ocean afternoon, white text Brand-navy dusk, thin Sunset Coral glow
/swap Brand sunset: Deep Hull into Sunset Coral and Lantern Gold Golden afterglow: Deep Hull, Lantern Gold low over the hills
/coins Purple into orange and Lantern Gold, golden harbour, Bitcoin balloon Violet twilight, crescent moon
Sky meets the header — every night sky starts at night navy #00193C so there is no seam under the header; day skies start at the page's own top colour.
Text on the sky — white on deep tops (/sell, /swap, /coins, all nights); Abyss Navy on the light /buy morning sky. Always WCAG AA.
Solid hills at night — the hills are drawn near-opaque so the sky gradient never shows through them; lit windows keep their warm lamp light.
Phones — the harbour drops away below 768px and only the sky shows; the page's own picture carries the message.
Phone browser colours — the phone's status bar takes the colour at the top of each page (landing sky, the page's header, the sign-in sky) and the area past the end of the page takes the colour at its foot, so the page runs edge to edge with no white or grey bands.
/coins is the one off-palette page — its purple-to-gold day and violet night are a deliberate showcase accent, approved 29 Oct 2026. Do not carry purple onto other pages.

Account pages — two places on the same coast

Sign in and Create account sit on their own pictures of the CoinPort coast, drawn in the landing harbour's style, behind the white card. Updated 31 Oct 2026.

Which page, which scene — Sign in, Forgot password, Reset password and Verify email: a bench on the clifftop path above the bay at sunrise. Create account: the harbour entrance from the breakwater, with the lighthouse and a sailboat, so its five selling points sit over open sky.
Dawn sky — the landing's own gradient, top to horizon: #0078F0 → #3F9CF4 (50%) → #A7D3F1 (78%) → #F5E2C2 (92%) → #FFD59F. The page above the picture carries on in the top colour, so there is never a seam.
Flat, crisp, no grain — flat fills and hard outlines like the landing's vector hills; faint ridges between hill layers are kept, painterly texture is not. Drawn 3072px wide so wide screens never stretch them soft.
One family of boats — only the white sailboat with its reflection, the landing's rowboat and its motor yacht (on a soft navy shadow). Boats further out are smaller; nothing nearer than the bench looks bigger than it should. No other boat styles.
Trees at believable scale — palms only on the shore and headland; never on the far hills, and never taller than the houses in front of them. No olive trees, cypresses or church towers.
Night — navy sky with the drawn star field, lit windows, a lamp by the bench; no moon.
Phones — a 3:4 crop of the same picture fills the screen edge to edge, no inset frame; the phone's status bar and the area past the end of the page take the sky colour at the top and the ground colour at the foot.
Logo — the usual Shoal Cyan keyhole on these pages, day and night (a darker tint was tried on 31 Oct and dropped).

Hero pictures — the flow, drawn

/sell — coins → CoinPort → PayID → your bank, with “+$350.00 AUD · Received just now” over the bank. /buy — the same run the other way: AUD notes → PayID → CoinPort → coins, “+247.18 USDT · In your wallet”.
Direction — streams fade in from where money starts (faint) to where it lands (strong); the gold PayID line carries an arrowhead.
PayID — the real PayID logo in navy on a white tag, sitting above its line; no lightning bolt, no speech bubble.
Keep it clean — no sparkles, stars or speed lines; the CoinPort tile has no ring or outline; shadows are a faint neutral navy, never a coloured blue.

Motion

Slow and ambient — things drift, they never dart. Everything holds still when the visitor has reduce motion turned on.
Loading — a navy screen with the CoinPort mark turning like a combination safe (4 turns right, 3 left, 2 right, 1 left, each stopping at a different point), then the Shoal Cyan keyhole turns green as “unlocked”, with “Loading CoinPort…”. Never a white page, never a spinning ring.
Seaplane (landing) — flies nose-first, right to left, about 18 s a pass, fading in and out at the ends. Never flies backwards.
Sailboat (landing horizon) — drifts left to right, opposite to the plane, about 70 s a crossing.
Rowboat (landing foreground) — bobs on a 4.5 s swell, a few px and about a degree; rope and shadow stay put.
Bitcoin balloon (/coins, day only) — small and hazed as if far off, a 16 s bob; replaced at night by a crescent moon with a soft glow.

Photography — do & don't

Do

  • Lead with Australian context — Melbourne CBD, Bourke St, Yarra, Sydney harbour, regional Vic.
  • Use natural light — soft morning or golden hour. Cool blue-toned daylight is fine.
  • Show real customers in unposed moments — ages 25 → 65, multi-cultural, casual.
  • Crop tight on hands holding phone with CoinPort UI visible. Show our product in context.
  • Treat warm tones to lean cooler — pull yellows toward neutral, lift shadows slightly.

Don't

  • No crypto cliches — Bitcoin coins on circuit boards, neon green Matrix code, lambos, rockets.
  • No hands holding glowing orbs or any AI-stock-photo aesthetic.
  • No staged trading floors, no men in suits at Bloomberg terminals.
  • Avoid heavily filtered, hyper-saturated, or Instagram-y treatments.
  • Never use celebrity, athlete, or influencer imagery without explicit licence.

Crop ratios

16:9Hero · video
4:3Card thumbs
1:1Social · OG
3:4Editorial
9:16Story · Reel

Layering with brand elements

Logo on photo — always use the white wordmark. Place over an area of even tone; add a 24px safe margin from edges. If the photo background is busy, add a subtle 30−50% dark gradient at the top.
Text on photo — use white at 92% opacity. Always meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) against the photo region.
No image-on-image — never sandwich illustration over photography or vice versa.
Attribution — bottom-right corner, 10px, white at 60% opacity, prefixed "Photo: ".
